title: Open problem on minimum independence ratio of Mycielski graphs
statement_text: The exact value of the minimum independence ratio $\mathrm{mir}(M_k)$ of the Mycielski graphs $M_k$ seems to be unknown.
context_text: The independence ratio of a graph $G$ is $\alpha(G)/|V(G)|$, and the minimum independence ratio $\mathrm{mir}(G)$ is the minimum independence ratio of an induced subgraph of $G$ with at least one vertex (its inverse is the Hall ratio). $M_k$ denotes the $k$-th Mycielski graph, obtained by iterating Mycielski's construction (from a graph $G$ on $v_1,\dots,v_n$, add copies $u_1,\dots,u_n$ with $u_i$ adjacent to the neighbours of $v_i$, and a new vertex adjacent to all $u_i$), normalized so that $M_2$ is the $5$-cycle; $M_k$ is triangle-free and $\chi(M_k)=k+1$. Every proper subgraph of $M_k$ is $k$-colourable, which gives $\mathrm{mir}(M_k)\ge\frac1k$ for $k\ge3$; so, unlike the case $k=2$ (minimum independence ratio at least $\frac12$ forces bipartiteness), a minimum independence ratio at least $\frac1k$ does not force chromatic number at most $k$. Cropper, Gyárfás and Lehel proved that every triangle-free graph is an induced subgraph of a Mycielski graph and deduced that there are $c_1,c_2>0$ with $c_1\frac{\sqrt{\log m}}{m}\le\mathrm{mir}(M_s)\le c_2\frac{\log m}{m}$ for every integer $m\ge3$, where $s$ is one less than the Ramsey number $R(3,m)=\Theta(m^2/\log m)$. The remark is made in passing, without a formal question.
notes: Stated informally in passing ('seems to be unknown'); no labelled environment. Question 1.2 is posed in the paper but immediately resolved negatively and so is not extracted as an open problem.
